subject: Upfront laddered prepay, ramp schedule, and tail payment options
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reopening: multi-year prepay structure and payment terms

Vanessa,

Thanks for the time last week — we had an internal alignment call and want to revisit the economics for a multi-year commit. Two asks from procurement and finance:

1) They prefer a laddered prepay (year 1 partial upfront, year 2 prepay on renewal) rather than a single full 24-month prepay.
2) They need flexible payment terms on the tail: specifically asking whether Redwood can accept Net90 on milestone invoices for year-two ramp payments.

High level: Acme is targeting a 2-year commitment at ~$1.2M ARR equivalent, but they want the first-year cash flow to be lighter — ideally 30% upfront, then milestone-based payments tied to usage/ramp. They also asked about term discount levels if we can agree to the laddered approach.

Can you share what packaging options and discount cadence you can offer? Also looping in procurement (cc) to keep them in the loop.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Data Platforms, Acme Health
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reopening: multi-year prepay structure and payment terms

Jordan — thanks for laying this out. I talked to Finance and Sales Ops this morning and sketched three options that aim to hit your cash-flow ask while keeping unit economics reasonable for both sides. Attaching a summarized proposal and an SOW workbook with ramp tranches. Attachment: Redwood-Proposal-Acme-20261011.pdf; SOW-Laddered-Commitments.xlsx

Option A — Conservative (Finance-friendly)
- 30% upfront at contract signature (covers onboarding + month 1 runrate)
- 40% due at 12 months (annual prepay for year 2)
- Remaining 30% paid at 18 months contingent on usage ramp targets
- Total term discount: 18% off list for 24-month commit
- Payment terms: Net60 on milestone invoices; Net90 considered only with PO and a signed amendment

Option B — Balanced (preferred)
- 50% upfront; 30% at 12 months; 20% at 18 months
- Total term discount: 24% off list
- Payment terms: Net60 standard; Net90 possible for year-two invoices with finance approval

Option C — Upfront-heavy (best pricing)
- 80% upfront; 20% at 12 months
- Total term discount: 30% off list
- Payment terms: Net30 on milestone invoices

Key notes:
- We can include a usage-ramp SLO in the SOW so that milestone payments are contingent on defined throughput/latency/consumption bands. That makes auditability easier for your procurement people.
- If Acme requires Net90 by default, we usually require a PO plus a one-time financing fee (1.25% of committed value) to offset receivable risk.

I've asked Marcus (cc) to confirm that the proposed ramp metrics are technically feasible for the profile you described. Monica and Rachel, I may need quick sign-off on whether we can waive the financing fee in special circumstances.

Next steps: Jordan, can you confirm which option aligns best with Acme's internal cash plan and whether procurement can provide a PO when we sign? If so, I’ll issue a revised proposal and a DS envelope for signature.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reopening: multi-year prepay structure and payment terms

Quick technical note on the ramp tranches:

- The SOW workbook's ramp triggers are based on 95th-percentile token throughput per minute and sustained daily active sessions. Those are measurable via our Console and can be exported monthly for audit.
- For the 18-month contingent tranche we recommend two simple gates: (a) 60% of forecasted token consumption reached for three consecutive months, OR (b) average inference latency maintained under agreed SLO while consumption increases.
- If you want milestone invoices tied more closely to feature rollout (e.g., production + integration milestones), we can add a small integration-credit that reduces the milestone amount if rollouts slip.

From an infra standpoint, all ramped capacity will be pinable to dedicated pools for SLA purposes. No technical blockers on the structure Vanessa proposed.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reopening: multi-year prepay structure and payment terms

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from procurement/finance:

1) We want the upfront to be 30% (Option A), but we also need Net90 on the 18-month contingent tranche (year-two ramp payment). Is Redwood willing to accept Net90 on that one tranche without a financing fee if Acme provides a signed PO at contract execution?

2) For auditability: can Redwood provide monthly export of consumption (csv) and an attestation that the exported numbers match what was billed? We need this to satisfy our internal controls.

3) If we move to Option A, what is the final term discount you can guarantee? You listed 18% — is there room to improve to ~20% if we commit to a 24-month auto-renewal clause?

We'd prefer to avoid an upfront 50% since our cash calendar is tight this year.

— Priya (Acme Procurement)
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: priya.suresh@acmehealth.com, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RE: Reopening: multi-year prepay structure and payment terms

Hi Priya & team — quick legal/finance check-in. We can accommodate Net90 on the single 18-month contingent invoice under the following conditions:

- Acme provides a signed PO at contract signature covering the committed amounts and a signed amendment to the Master Subscription Agreement specifying Net90 for that specific tranche.
- If Net90 extends beyond 90 days (e.g., delays to 120+), Redwood reserves the right to assess a late fee calculated on the outstanding amount (per MSA) unless otherwise agreed.
- Regarding the financing fee: given this is a strategic healthcare customer, Finance is prepared to waive the 1.25% receivable fee only if Acme agrees to a 24-month auto-renewal at the same rate and provides an initial PO for the first 12 months.

On the attestation/export: we can provide monthly CSV exports from Redwood Console and a Redwood-generated consumption reconciliation report. We can include a simple attestation clause in the SOW acknowledging that exported numbers will be the authoritative consumption figure for milestone gating.

Rachel, please confirm operationally that we can produce the monthly CSV and the reconciliation attestation.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@acmehealth.com>, Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Revised laddered prepay proposal and next steps

Priya/Jordan — appreciate the clarity. To summarize the agreement in-principle and next steps so procurement can move to PO: 

Agreed commercial terms (in-principle)
- Option chosen: Option A (Conservative laddered prepay) with one concession: Redwood will increase the term discount from 18% to 20% if Acme agrees to a 24-month auto-renewal clause at execution.
- Upfront: 30% at signature.
- Year 2: 40% at 12 months.
- Contingent tranche: 30% at 18 months tied to the SOW ramp gates. That 18-month tranche will be invoiced with Net90, provided Acme issues a PO at signing and signs the Net90 amendment.
- Financing fee: waived conditional on the 24-month auto-renewal and 12-month PO as described by Monica.
- Audit/export: Redwood will provide monthly CSV exports + a monthly reconciliation attestation.

Attachments: I have uploaded the revised proposal to the DocuSign envelope and attached the SOW workbook for your procurement team to review (see attachments). DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/servlet/documents?id=ABCDEF-2026-10-acme

Next steps for Acme procurement:
1) Confirm PO issuance for year 1 (covers 30% upfront) — PO number to be added to the DS envelope.
2) Review and confirm the SOW ramp gates (we can do a 30-minute session to walk Marcus's ramp definitions).
3) Sign the DS envelope and send the PO. Once received, Rachel will schedule invoice generation and Monica will countersign the Net90 amendment.

If that works, I’ll have the amended proposal issued today and route the DocuSign link to Jordan and your procurement mailbox.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
